names.note: Read out of saint.gr's line for 29 Ιουλίου, «Άγιος Ιωάννης ο στρατιώτης», with the rank word and the trade left off. The 12 Ιουνίου line prints the same name with the epithet capitalised, «ο Στρατιώτης».

source.text: saint.gr, το εορτολόγιο της 29ης Ιουλίου — «Άγιος Ιωάννης ο στρατιώτης»

attestations.note: The life page heads «Τύπος εορτής: Σταθερή. Εορτάζει στις 29 Ιουλίου εκάστου έτους», the same day as the listing, and carries the only life either day has: the soldier of the Taifali under Julian the Apostate who hunted Christians in appearance and helped them in secret, buried in the Pandektes. No asterisk, no «Δεν είναι διασταυρωμένη» sentence, no hymn.

source.text: saint.gr, το εορτολόγιο της 12ης Ιουνίου — «Άγιος Ιωάννης ο Στρατιώτης»

attestations.note: The second Greek day, kept as «Άγιος Ιωάννης ο Στρατιώτης». Its page prints no life at all — «Δεν έχουμε λεπτομέρειες για τον βίο του Αγίου Ιωάννη του Στρατιώτη», we have no details of the life of Saint John the Soldier — only the name, the trade and a couplet. The corpus held it as a second folder, and the 29 Ιουλίου folder said outright that it “says nothing about whether the two are one man”. The author ruled on 3 October 2026 that they are one, and this record is the merge; no year, no place, no emperor and no hymn come with the day, because the page has none to give.
Not checked: days.pravoslavie.ru for the corresponding Julian day (1 October 2026).
Not checked: doxologia.ro's calendar for the same civil day (1 October 2026).

source.text: Православни подсетник (pravoslavno.rs), Охридски пролог за 12.08.2026 (30. јул ст. ст.) — „Св. Јован војник.“

attestations.note: The day's fourth entry. The identification is past doubt and is the whole of the folder's dossier: the secret Christian soldier sent by Julian the Apostate to kill Christians who instead helped them hide, imprisoned at Constantinople, freed at the tyrant's death, and invoked for the finding of thieves. The serbian row was `undocumented`, so the row lands here. **A DAY NO OTHER CALENDAR KEEPS HIM ON**: the two greek rows on this folder are 29 July and 12 June and this book puts him on the Julian 30 July — the Prologue's own 29 July page was read in this same block and does not name him, printing Callinicus, Serapheima, Theodota and Eustathius of Mtskheta — so 30 July is the day of the page actually read and the row stands on it. `types` UNTOUCHED: «војник» is the `soldier` held. `dates` UNTOUCHED: the folder's `floruit` is «under Julian the Apostate» and the entry names that emperor and gives no year, closing only «Упокојио се мирно у старости», he reposed in peace in old age — an age is not a year and nothing was narrowed. NO `locations`. NO NEW `related`: `john-the-theologian` is already here and untouched, and the entry names nobody but the emperor. NO SERBIAN NAME FORM WAS STORED, AND THAT IS A DELIBERATE REFUSAL: the heading „Св. Јован војник.“ gives «Св.», which is not a rank, «војник», which BRIEF-SERBIAN §5 reads as the rank `soldier` and which §6 keeps out of a stored form, and no by-name, no place and no see — so the bare «Јован» was the only form there was, and `fk.mjs` returns ELEVEN other holders of it. The brief says to refuse the form rather than widen a fold, and this is the 12-24 `nicholas-from-the-soldiers` refusal in the same words, his heading's only other word having likewise been a rank. WHAT THE BOOK ADDS: that prayers to him help thieves to be found, «Молитве њему помажу да се пронађу лопови», and that after his death he appeared to some who had need of his help. The Prologue prints no hymn (8 October 2026).

floruit.note: saint.gr: «Ο Άγιος Ιωάννης έζησε στα χρόνια του Ιουλιανού του Παραβάτη (361)». That one year is all the page prints; it gives no year of birth and none of death, and the bounds here are its single figure rather than the length of the reign.
